[[piv:gate]]
Re-reading the vocabulary to adversarially verify names/props/enums before writing.

Gate check passed. I re-read the vocabulary's `metric-tile` and `list-row` entries: both are explicitly "Library-generic — cross-scenario" primitives (not scoped to Verdant), and `list-row`'s usage text even cites the exact Northwind-style example ("Pallet wrap, 23 micron — 85 units short") confirming intended use here. Props I'm using — `label`, `value` (string), `unit`, `meta`, `status` (free text, no enum), `tone` (enum: neutral/warn/critical) — all match exactly, and neither component declares children, so I correctly omit `children`. Tone values I plan (`neutral`, `warn`, `critical`) are all valid enum members. Labels ("Updated today", "Oversold as of today", "Thin cover as of today", "Total oversold shortfall") each read the state without depending on tone; each list-row's entity name + status pill + unit phrase together read the state per the primitive's documented pattern. I deliberately excluded `demo-notice` — it's scenario-honesty chrome, not part of the analytical answer, and would dilute the focused single-question read the slot demands. I'm listing only the 3 named SKUs that are oversold (the entire risk set, not a per-record dump of the 22-row table) — consistent with "never one node per record." Node count is 7, under the 8-node cap.

Computed figures verified against fixtures: most recent `updatedOn` = 2026-07-19, held by 6 SKUs (sku-03, 07, 10, 14, 16, 21). Of those, 3 are `oversold` (sku-03, 10, 16 — which are in fact the *only* 3 oversold SKUs in the whole 22-row dataset) and 3 are `low`. Shortfalls (committed − onHand): sku-03 Pallet wrap 23 micron = 145−60=85; sku-16 Wooden pallet, EUR = 410−340=70; sku-10 Stretch film hand 400% = 130−90=40. Sum = 195. This is the real "what changed most recently and what it means": today's refresh is exactly where every current oversell lives.

The validator confirms the composition is structurally sound against the real vocabulary — every component name, prop, and enum value resolves.

Summary of the panel: it opens with the scope of the most recent update batch (6 SKUs touched today, 2026-07-19), splits that batch into its two risk tiers (3 newly oversold, 3 running thin), names the three oversold SKUs individually with their exact shortfalls (the full oversold set in the dataset, not a table dump), and closes with the aggregate shortfall (195 units) an operator would need to clear across purchase orders. The read this supports: the dashboard's most recent refresh is precisely where all current oversell risk lives — nothing older is hiding a worse problem, but these three lines need action now.
